findings.claim: L1 exam tip: 'Context (AO4) must be embedded naturally'. L1 content: 'Understanding this context is essential for the Eduqas C720U Component 1 exam.' L8 content: 'AO3/AO4 (context): Embed Elizabethan/Jacobean context into your analysis where it is credited', with the paragraph pattern ending 'Effect on audience > Context'. L8 exam tip: 'Always embed context within your analysis'. L8 content: 'Context must be embedded, not bolted on.'
findings.truth: AO4 is accurate vocabulary, sentence structure, spelling and punctuation. AO3 (context) is not assessed on the Shakespeare section at all. The unit repeatedly sends students after marks that do not exist and builds a paragraph template around them. Rewritten to name the three real objectives and to say context is used only to work out what a line means.
findings.evidence: spec 2.1: 'Section A (20%) Shakespeare (40 marks) ... one extract-based question and one essay question on the text as a whole ... Section A assesses AO1, AO2 and AO4.' AO4 is defined as 'Use a range of vocabulary and sentence structures for clarity, purpose and effect, with accurate spelling and punctuation.' AO3 (context) appears only for Section B poetry and for Component 2. A grep of the spec for a per-question mark figure returns only the four 40-mark section totals and the AO percentage table.

findings.claim: L7: 'Shakespeare wrote for the Globe Theatre'. L1: 'For the Elizabethan audience at the Globe, Juliet's refusal to marry Paris was shocking'.
findings.truth: Romeo and Juliet was written around 1594-96 and the 1597 First Quarto already says it had 'been often (and with great applause) plaid publiquely'. The Lord Chamberlain's Men played it at The Theatre or the Curtain. The Globe was not built until 1599, so no first audience saw it there. Corrected to an open-air London playhouse, with the Globe date given.
findings.evidence: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Romeo_and_Juliet - composition c.1591-95, Q1 1597 title page 'often (and with great applause) plaid publiquely', Lord Chamberlain's Men at The Theatre or the Curtain; Globe opened 1599.

findings.claim: 'Eduqas', 'Eduqas C720U' or 'Eduqas C720U Component 1' appears in student-facing text in all eight lessons: L1 content x3 and exam tip, L2 content x2 and exam tip, L3 content and exam tip, L4 exam tip, L5 content and exam tip, L6 content and exam tip, L7 exam tip, L8 description, conclusion, exam tip, two knowledge checks and a flashcard.
findings.truth: House rule for Eduqas/WJEC lessons: prose, questions, tips and flashcards never name the board, and spec codes are a banned string. All 19 places reworded neutrally ('the exam', 'Part (i)', 'the Shakespeare section', 'the first Shakespeare question').
findings.evidence: CHECK_PROMPT banned-string list; Eduqas/WJEC neutral-phrasing house rule.

findings.claim: Practice question 3: 'Read the extract from Act 3, Scene 5, from “Hang thee, young baggage, disobedient wretch!” to “Or I will drag thee on a hurdle thither.”'
findings.truth: The two cue lines are the wrong way round: 'Or I will drag thee on a hurdle thither' comes twelve lines BEFORE 'Hang thee young baggage, disobedient wretch!'. A student following the instruction cannot find the extract. Re-cued forwards, from Capulet's 'How now, how now, chopp'd logic?' to 'For, by my soul, I'll ne'er acknowledge thee', which still contains 'baggage', 'wretch' and the hurdle threat named in the mark scheme.
findings.evidence: Unit text file, 3.5: l.3715 'Or I will drag thee on a hurdle thither.'; l.3727 'Hang thee young baggage, disobedient wretch!'; l.3781 'For by my soul, I'll ne'er acknowledge thee,'.

findings.claim: Key fact: 'What's in a name? That which we call a rose / By any other word would smell as sweet'. Knowledge check 3: 'By any other _____ would smell as sweet' with options name / word / title / label and 'word' marked correct.
findings.truth: The knowledge check marks 'name' wrong. Our text of the play, and this unit's own Lesson 3 flashcard, both read 'By any other name would smell as sweet'. ('word' is the Second Quarto reading, printed by some editions, which is exactly why it could not stay as a wrong answer alongside 'name'.) Key fact corrected to 'name', the answer index moved to 'name', and the 'word' option replaced with a clean distractor.
findings.evidence: Unit text file l.1586 'By any other name would smell as sweet;'. Lesson 3 flashcard 2 already reads 'name'.

findings.claim: Practice question 5: 'Read Act 2, Scene 3 from “Within the infant rind of this weak flower” to “And vice sometime by action dignified.”'
findings.truth: Reversed again: 'And vice sometime's by action dignified' comes four lines BEFORE 'Within the infant rind of this weak flower'. Re-cued forwards from 'Virtue itself turns vice, being misapplied' to 'Poison hath residence, and medicine power', which keeps both the virtue/vice couplet and the poison/medicine antithesis the mark scheme asks for.
findings.evidence: Unit text file 2.3: l.1882-83 'Virtue itself turns vice being misapplied, / And vice sometime's by action dignified.'; l.1887-88 'Within the infant rind of this weak flower / Poison hath residence, and medicine power:'.

findings.claim: Of Juliet's Act 4, Scene 3 soliloquy: 'seeing “Tybalt's bloody corpse” in its “bloody sheet.” The repetition of “bloody” links the tomb to violence and death.'
findings.truth: 'Bloody sheet' is Romeo's line at the tomb in Act 5, Scene 3 - a quotation from a different scene and a different speaker put into Juliet's mouth. Her soliloquy says 'bloody Tybalt, yet but green in earth, / Lies festering in his shroud' and uses 'bloody' once, so there is no repetition to analyse. Corrected to her actual words.
findings.evidence: Unit text file: l.4234-35 (Juliet 4.3) 'Where bloody Tybalt, yet but green in earth, / Lies festering in his shroud'; l.4934 (Romeo 5.3) 'Tybalt, liest thou there in thy bloody sheet?'.

findings.claim: 'in the aubade, she engages in stichomythia that shows her as Romeo's intellectual equal'
findings.truth: The aubade is built from speeches of five to ten lines each, not single-line exchanges, so it is not stichomythia. The stichomythia is in the shared sonnet at the ball, where Romeo and Juliet alternate single lines - which is what this unit's own Lesson 6 flashcard says. A student writing 'stichomythia' about the aubade would lose the AO2 point.
findings.evidence: Unit text file 3.5 l.3455-3495: Juliet 5 lines, Romeo 6, Juliet 5, Romeo 9, Juliet 10. Shared sonnet 1.5 l.1312-1325: single-line alternation.

findings.claim: Practice question 1: 'Read Act 2, Scene 2 from “But soft, what light through yonder window breaks?” to “As a rich jewel in an Ethiope's ear.”' with a mark scheme rewarding the 'jewel simile'.
findings.truth: 'As a rich jewel in an Ethiop's ear' is Act 1, Scene 5, not Act 2, Scene 2, so the extract cannot run to it. Re-cued to 'As daylight doth a lamp', which ends the star passage in the same Act 2, Scene 2 speech, and the mark scheme's 'jewel simile' replaced with the lamp comparison that is actually in the extract.
findings.evidence: Unit text file: l.1224 'As a rich jewel in an Ethiop's ear;' (1.5); l.1532 'But soft, what light through yonder window breaks?' and l.1549-50 'The brightness of her cheek would shame those stars, / As daylight doth a lamp' (2.2).

findings.claim: L8 exam tip: 'Both are worth 20 marks.' L8 knowledge check 2: 'How many marks is each part of the Eduqas Shakespeare question worth?' answer '20 marks each'. L8 flashcard 12: 'Part (i) extract analysis (20m) and Part (ii) whole-text on theme or character (20m).'
findings.truth: The spec states no per-question mark split for Section A - only 40 marks for the whole section. A 20+20 split is a reasonable teaching assumption but is not verifiable, so it should not be taught as fact. All three places also carried the board name (F3), so the numberless rewrite rode along with those edits: the tip now says 'Together they are worth 40 marks', the knowledge check now asks for the section total (40 marks, the figure the spec does give) and the flashcard says '40 marks together'.

findings.claim: Fifteen top-band mark-scheme descriptors across lessons 1-6 and 8 end with 'Embeds context', 'Embeds context throughout', 'Embeds Elizabethan context about fathers' rights' or 'Embeds patriarchal context'.
findings.truth: Read as band criteria these imply context is credited on a section that assesses AO1, AO2 and AO4 only. Left alone to stay consistent with the macbeth and othello units, which kept context references inside mark schemes and fixed only the stated exam rules. Worth a fleet decision rather than a one-unit change.

findings.claim: 'Romeo and Juliet share a sonnet at their first meeting (Act 1, Scene 5, lines 95-108)' - the same numbering in Lesson 2.
findings.truth: Line numbering for 1.5 differs by edition (the sonnet is 92-105, 93-106 or 104-117 in the common ones). The act and scene are right and the two lessons agree with each other, so no edit.
findings.evidence: Unit text file carries no line numbering; standard editions disagree.

findings.claim: 'As a rich jewel in an Ethiope's ear'
findings.truth: Our text and most modern editions spell it 'Ethiop's'. A spelling variant found in older editions; not mark-affecting, so left alone.
findings.evidence: Unit text file l.1224 'As a rich jewel in an Ethiop's ear;'.

findings.claim: Every mark scheme in the unit ends its ladder 'Lower-mid band (5-8) ... Lower band (1-4)'.
findings.truth: The house ladder names the bottom rungs 'Low band' and 'Basic band'. 'Lower band' is not a banned string and the board's numbered ladder is nowhere in this unit, so no rebuild was needed. Flagged only so the fleet can normalise the wording later.

summary: The unit's root error is its exam-technique advice: AO4 is defined as context and context is taught as credited, when the Shakespeare section assesses AO1, AO2 and AO4 only. That runs through lessons 1 and 8, and the board name or spec code appears in student-facing text in all eight lessons (19 places, including two knowledge checks and a flashcard). On the play itself the writing is sound: the real errors are a knowledge check that marks 'By any other name' wrong, Romeo's Act 5 'bloody sheet' put into Juliet's Act 4 soliloquy, stichomythia located in the aubade, the Globe named as the play's theatre nine years before it was built, and three practice extracts whose cue lines are reversed or drawn from the wrong scene. 39 edits.
